articles.title: 'We Don't Take Anything For Granted' — LATAM is the Strongest Region in Street Fighter 6, and It’s Because They’re Hungrier Than You
articles.summary: IGN sat down with Blaz and the team at 2Game to discuss their monumental victory at the Street Fighter League Americas 2026 Finals and that viral set with NoahTheProdigy.
articles.body:
If you haven’t watched the Street Fighter League Americas 2026 Finals , you’re missing out. It is — and I say this with complete sincerity — some of the best competitive Street Fighter I have ever seen in my life, mostly owing to a heart-stopping set between Derek ‘Blaz’ and Noah ‘NoahTheProdigy’ Solis.

Blaz, a 17-year-old Chilean phenom, broke into the scene with a bang when he was just 14 years old. At 15, he got second place at Capcom Cup — the world’s most competitive Street Fighter tournament — and at 16, he secured third place. During this time, Latin America as a region became extremely strong in Street Fighter 6 , with figures like 15-year-old Chilean player Craime making Top 8 at Evo Las Vegas this year and winning the 2026 Esports World Cup for the game.

LATAM’s strength showed itself in spades at the Street Fighter League Americas Finals this year. Blaz and his team 2Game, made up of players from Mexico, Argentina, and Brazil, plowed through the competition, culminating in a breathtaking Grand Finals set that had viewers at the edge of their seats. Blaz, using Jamie (a wildly underrepresented character in competitive Street Fighter) and NoahTheProdigy, using Luke, duked it out in a thrilling back-and-forth brawl that saw Blaz perfect parry three times in a row on just a sliver of health against Luke’s projectiles.

This set was something else 👀 #SFLAMERICAS2026 | — Capcom Fighters (@CapcomFighters) November 9, 2026

This set was something else 👀 #SFLAMERICAS2026

It was nothing short of jaw-dropping, and Blaz — refusing to switch to Ryu or Sagat, his usual picks — clutched out the win. After a short break, Mexican player Lugabo secured the victory, giving 2Game the comeback they’d been working so hard for after their 3rd place finish last year.

I got the chance to speak with 2Game’s talent backstage in the aftermath of their monumental achievement, where I asked the obvious question: Why is Latin America so good in Street Fighter right now?

“I mean, we don’t take anything for granted,” the team’s coach told me. “That’s why. We don’t have as many opportunities as anyone else, and that's why we’ve got to do whatever we can in any possible way to make sure we play at the highest level, no matter what. That's why we're doing everything we can with any opportunity. Lugabo, for example — this is the third time he's played offline, and he's already that good. It shows we have a lot of hidden talent in Latin America since forever, at least for the past 15 years, but many of them don't have the opportunity to travel. So what you're seeing right now is what happens when we get the chance.”

At 17 years old, Blaz’s achievements remind me fondly of Victor ‘Punk’ Woodley’s first breakout into the scene back in the early days of Street Fighter V . Now more than ever, Street Fighter 6 seems geared toward a generation of younger competitors — but for Blaz, it isn’t one’s age or ‘young man reactions’ that matter.

“What's important for Blaz is not about age, but specifically about knowledge, experience, and how much you can get from playing,” his coach said, translating on Blaz’s behalf.

Of course, I had to ask him about that standout set against NoahTheProdigy, which has since gone viral within the fighting game community and sparked inevitable comparisons to Daigo ‘TheBeast’ Umehara.

“I came into the Noah match thinking it was going to be a little bit easy, but I was a little bit surprised by how Noah played," Blaz explained. "He played a lot more focused on pressure, and it caught me off guard, but one of the things that you need to be able to do at these levels is to never surrender. So I did just that."

For now, 2Game is going home to continue their training in preparation for the Street Fighter League World Championships at Capcom Cup next year. I have to wonder how Blaz will fare as an individual player at this tournament; wildly, it makes me consider the very real possibility that he could win both Capcom Cup and Street Fighter League under 2Game’s banner. We’ll just have to wait and see, but it seems that Blaz’s skills are only growing stronger by the day. And if his latest performance is anything to go by, it’s looking more likely than ever that fighting game fans are in for one hell of a treat.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Disaster in Zora Domain - Ice Cavern Dungeon Walkthrough - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains
articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains the same, there's plenty of new differences to be found while exploring Hyrule. Now that the Fire Temple has been cleansed and the Sage of Fire awakened, Link must find a way into the Water Temple below Lake Hylia. To reach it, you'll first need the ability to walk underwater with Iron Boots, and a new tunic to breathe underwater, which will lead you to seek out the Zora and a strange new Ice Cavern.

It's been seven years since Link last visited Zora Domain, and a bitter wind now blows down from Zora River. Something has happened to the Zora people, causing the flow of water to stop, and Lake Hylia to dry up as a result. Now that Link has more tools under his belt, it's time to revisit the source of Hyrule's waterways.

Heading up the path from Hyrule Field, you'll find the river a lot colder and gloomier than you may remember, but not much else has really changed. The Bean Seller is gone, and if you planted your first Magic Bean next to him, it's now grown into a floating magic plant you can ride to bypass a lot of the river if you want (as well as grabbing a Heart Piece on a high ledge by the central island if you missed it as a child).

Before moving on to the Zora entrance, be sure to stop by on the large raised island in the middle (the floating plant helps here). When night falls, head to the ledge on the southern side, and look back to the west. A Gold Skulltula will appear on a high wall that you can hit with your Hookshot.

Simiilarly, when you reach the falls in front of the Zora Domain entrance, look back along the high walls to the west to spot another Gold Skulltula lurking at night. It's pretty far off, so stand on the edge of the balcony along the stairs to hit it with your Hookshot.

Entering Zora Domain, you'll soon see the reason why there's no water flowing to Lake Hylia anymore: the place is frozen solid! A chill freeze has taken hold of the domain, and all of the Zora have seemingly vanished (or possibly frozen under the ice)! Even the Zora Shop is completely inaccessible!

Head up the long stairway, and you'll find the last remaining Zora, King Zora himself, is now trapped in a strange block of glowing red ice. This is no normal freeze, and will obviously take something strong to cure him.

While you're in King Zora's audience chamber, be sure to head down the side path north to the frozen waterfall. We highly recommend against trying to perform a dive under these conditions, but if you look to the left, there's a Gold Skulltula crawling along the wall high up here that you can still reach with your Hookshot.

An even colder breeze seems to be coming from just past King Zora, and as long as he's moved aside, you can slip past him up to Zora Fountain.

It's not clear what happened to Lord Jabu-Jabu, but in his place is a large collection of icebergs covering the frigid lake. One fairly large icy section actually forms a winding bridge at curves up north where the entrance to an icy cave looms large. Just be careful to keep your footing as you try to cross and deflect attacks from nearby Octoroks.

Along the icy bridge leading to the nearby cave, look for a small collection of icy platforms along the water leading further east. Move carefully by jumping across them and regaining your footing, and stop to deflect any incoming attacks. On the far side of these platforms, you can find a Piece of Heart on the last big platform for you to take.

Though not as big or intricate as the temples you've explored, the Ice Cavern is still a dangerous place to traverse. As wonderous as it is deadly, the entire cavern is coated in slippery ice that will have you scrambling to keep your footing when dealing with threats.

Be wary and move slowly through the corridors here, as icy stalagtites will often drop from the ceiling as you approach, but if you move slow they'll land with a crash far before you reach them.

Up ahead, you'll encounter more objects covered in the strange red ice, and you'll want to make a note of their locations for when you find a way to remove this particular problem.

At the far end of the corridor, the cavern will expand into a large icy arena where several spike traps bounce along the floor between three new enemies called Freezards. These ice foes will slide a little along the ice to get closer to you, before emitting a freezing breath with a surprising amount of reach!

The good news is that preparing their frosty breath locks them in place, and they can't swivel to face you and adjust their attacks. Their also very susceptible to being hookshotted, and melted in a flash from a little Din's Fire.

Did you know their freeze breath works on more than just Link? Angle yourself so there's a moving spike trap between you and the Freezard, and they'll freeze it solid to render the spikes harmless for a short duration!

Once the Freezards are destroyed, a large gate will open, allowing you head up the next winding corridor. Move slowly to avoid the falling hazards above until you enter the next room.

In the next large cavern, you'll come upon a large spinning scythe trap made of icy blades. A large gate on the far end is tied to five silver Rupees that have scattered across the room at different spots, and you'll need to collect them all to open the gate (Sadly, they don't translate into monetary gain).

First, carefully drop down the ledge and dart to the left to find a large wall of icy stalagmites on the ground you can slash apart to reveal a silver Rupee behind them.

The next three silver Rupees can all be found around the spinning scythe trap itself. It can look daunting, but try to line up a straight shot to run and jump while moving in a general counter-clockwise direction -- you don't want to be leaping into incoming blades, nor do you want to leap directly toward the middle of the trap, so angle your movement to pass by it instead, and move away from the blades to adjust your next dash accordingly.

Finally, climb up the ledges on the north side, then look for the fifth silver Rupee just off the ledge that you can jump back south (after a blade has passed) to unseal the gate).

When looking at the floating silver Rupee high up off the ledge, you'll be facing south to the other end of the cavern. On a high wall above the row of stalagmites down below, is a Gold Skulltula you can claim with a Hookshot when you move under it.

In the new room to the north, you'll find another large ice sheet on the ground, with a series of stone structure you can climb to some guarded treasure up above.

In addition to Freezards patrolling the ice, you'll also have to deal with the threat of Ice Keese flying above. They'll freeze you solid if they slam into you (unless you have a shield ready), so take them out first from a distance using your Bow before advancing to the stone platforms.

Hookshot up to the Freezard on the raised platform to take him out quickly, and then jump across north to find a strange icy structure backed by red ice. Slice the stalagmite apart and a font of eerie Blue Fire will spread out, melting all the nearby red ice away! Several motes will dance around the newly opened "fountain" allowing you to bottle Blue Fire!

If you can empty at least two of your bottles and keep them stocked with Blue Fire as much as possible. You can melt some red ice on a lower platform to the southeast to find a Blue Rupee in a pot, and then head up a high path to the northwest.

Hookshot to or dodge around the Freezard protecting another hunk of red ice, and melt it away with Blue Fire to reveal a large Treasure Chest holding the Dungeon Map for this area!

With at least two bottles of Blue Fire, head back into the previous cavern room with the spinning scythes, and head left to the east, melting away some red ice blocking a corridor.

This path leads to more spike traps and a Freezard who can freeze them for you. Move beyond him toward the end of this corridor to find three small alcoves: One to the north is covered in red ice, and hides some pots with Rupees, as well as Fairy Thoughts that yearn for the warmth of the sun (Play the Sun's Song to get healed by Fairy Essence!).

The southern alcove has another font of Blue Fire you can re-bottle your two empty bottles with, leaving the far eastern alcove. Slash aside the stalagmites and watch for Keese that spring out to locate another large Treasure Chest holding the Compass!

After claiming the Compass from the eastern corridor, turn around from the chest without running back. Hidden on the other side of a low icy column by the chest on the northern side is a Gold Skulltula you can claim with your Hookshot.

Bottle up at least three motes of Blue Fire, and then head back to the spinning scythe room. Be sure to backtrack for a moment back down toward the entrance. There were several early chunks of red ice you passed earlier that you can now melt:

Two chunks of red ice by where you first fought some Freezards along the spike traps have pots have a Red Rupee and a Fairy inside.

The furthest chunk of red ice also has a pot with a Magic Jar inside.

Refill at least two more bottles of Blue Fire, and use it to douse the other passageway from the main ice scythe room leading west this time.

Across a small gap, you can spot a large room several blocks and pillars spread out across an icy floor. Five silver Rupees have been spread out along the room, but some are on pillars too high to reach. To help you out, there's a short ice block that you can push, causing it to slide across the length of the room until it hits something.

Take out the Ice Keese in the room first to get rid of distractions, and then push the block west so that it hits a tall pillar with the first silver Rupee you can climb up to grab.

Next, push the ice block to the north, so that its lands just under a ledge full of red ice. Climb up and melt it all away to reveal a second silver Rupee.

Push the block to the side, so that it slides into either pit, and it will reform back where you first encountered it. You can now push the block south to reach a another tall pillar where you can clim up to reach the third Silver Rupee.

From the eastern side of the icy platform, look up across the gap you walked around when entering the room to find a Gold Skulltula on a high wall. You'll need to get close to the ledge without sliding over to use your Hookshot on it.

Push the ice block to the west again, and it will slide along until it hits one more tall pillar, which has a the fourth silver Rupee on it, and the fifth can be found on a lower platform just to the right.

Note that there's also a high alcove holding another font of Blue Fire in the western corner, and a ledge close by in the northwest corner has a familiar symbol at the edge. Push the ice block north, west, south, and west again to land right under the Blue Fire font, allowing you to climb up. You can then play the Song of Time to reveal a line of blue blocks connecting to the northwest ledge, where you'll find a small Treasure Chest holding a Red Rupee.

To enter the gate that was recently unsealed, reset the ice block by pushing it into a pit, then push the newly formed one south, west, north, east, and south to land under the ledge that you can climb up and head down the southern corridor.

Defeat the Freezards, and then look for one final piece of red ice blocking the doorway. If you forgot to grab some in the previous room, there's a high alcove to the east that has yet another font of Blue Fire to help you out.

In this last room, you'll face a mini-dungeon's mini-boss: The White Wolfos.

You can think them as a more powerful Wolfos that deal ice damage with their claws. Getting hit by them will freeze you in place while they unleash their double slash attack, so you'll either have to be very diligent about having your shield raised, or do your best to avoid their attack entirely.

Like the other Wolfos you've faced, the key to the first is letting theme swing wildly while you evade the attack entirely. This will cause them to overswing, spinning them in place and leaving their back exposed to several strikes.

Get in your hits after dodging their two-strike swings and then backpedal to wait for their next attack. With a bit of patience, the monster will fall, and reveal your reward for completing this dungeon: The Iron Boots!

With this item, you can now sink down to the bottom of watery areas to access areas even your swimming ability couldn't get you! You'll move slowly, but it can also be equally helpful for getting firm footing on unstable ground or in gusty winds.

As you grab your reward, Sheik will appear to brief you on the situation: All but one of the Zora have been frozen under the ice. Sheik was able to rescue Princess Ruto, who forged on ahead to the Water Temple to try and free her people from this icy curse. To reach the temple quickly, Sheik will have a new melody to bestow upon you.

Follow the prompt, and you'll learn the Serenade of Water, which teleports you to the large island in the middle of Lake Hylia!

Before you make the trip however, there's one other Zora who could use your help, and in doing so you'll be helping yourself. Head to the south to locate a pool of water leading to the exit, and be sure to grab at least one bottle of Blue Fire before you jump down into the water.

Equip the Iron Boots by pressing down on the D-Pad, and you'll sink like a rock to the bottom, allowing you to walk out of the tunnel and back to Zora Fountain.

As you return to Zora Fountain, know that much like walking through Death Mountain Crater without the Goron Tunic, trying to walk around underwater without a certain other tunic will slowly deal damage as Link runs out of air.

Unequip the boots to float back to the surface, and then head back into the Domain. Approach King Zora and drop some Blue Fire to melt the poor guy. He'll request that once again you help out his dear daughter in her quest to the Water Temple, and this time he has a special reward for you, the Zora Tunic! You'll now be able to breathe underwater indefinitely, as long as you have the stylish blue tunic equipped when also putting on the Iron Boots!

Now that you have the ability to go underwater as you please, try it out by returning back to the Zora Fountain. Equip the Iron Boots and the Zora Tunic, and then wade into the large pool of water. It's surprisingly deep, and along the bottom of the fountain you'll find a ring of shining Rupees around a Piece of Heart to claim!

Use the Seranade of Water to teleport yourself over to Lake Hylia. The dried up lake still has a sizeable pool of water protecting the entrance to the temple itself below, but before heading in, there's bit more prep you can do.

Start by heading back over to the northern side. Despite the lake drying up, the Fishing Hole is actually still open for business, and you can reach it either by taking the magic floating plant from the Laboratory, or standing below the docks and playing the Scarecrow Song to summon Pierre to zip up to the Fishing Hole entrance.

Much like when you were a Child, there's a prize for catching a big fish and setting a record. You'll need to find one over 60 cm, and they usually appear near the center of the pond (Fish seem to get more active when it rains, too...).

Carefully move out toward the middle to spy a big fish and cast your line. You may have to maneuver around a few smaller fries that want your lure first before you get attract the biggest fish's attention. Once its hooked, keep pulling in the direction the fish is going until it gets tired and stops moving, then reel it in!

Hooking the biggest fish will set a new record, awarding you a Golden Scale! An upgrade over the Silver Scales given by the Zora, this will let you dive down a total of 9 ft!

Now that you have the Golden Scales, return to the Lakeside Laboratory to show off your diving skills to the scientist. Dive the full way down (without the Iron Boots) and then talk to him. He'll be so impressed, he'll hand over a Piece of Heart!

Next, put on the Iron Boots and descend down to the bottom. There's a few things down here to admire, like some Rupees, a disarmingly empty cage (or not!), and a wooden crate you can roll into to reveal a Gold Skulltula that's been hiding underwater.

Now you'll be all caught up on all the upgrades you need before delving into the next dungeon. When you're ready to proceed, sink into the pool of water in front of the temple entrance below the island at the center of Lake Hylia, and use your Hookshot on the target above the gate. This will unseal the entrance, giving you access to the Water Temple dungeon.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's High-Quality Visuals Have Players Second-Guessing Decades of Memories
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake gives Link's first 3D adventure a new coat of paint, but some of its details have players second-guessing the reality they thought they once knew.
articles.body:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake gives Link's first 3D adventure a new coat of paint, but some of its details have players second-guessing the reality they thought they once knew.

You don't have to be a Zelda expert to know what fairies look like in the original Ocarina of Time. Navi is an icon, which means most people who have ever even thought about touching one of the games in Nintendo's beloved fantasy franchise know that Link's little guide is little more than a glowing ball with wings – or so they thought.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time brought more than just a fancy new tunic for Link when it made the leap to Switch 2 last week. A few close-up shots early in the adventure make one shocking fact clear: The fairies of Kokiri Forest aren't orbs of light – they're fuzzy .

It's the kind of detail the original Nintendo 64 release could have never conveyed made real thanks to the artists at Nintendo and the power of the Switch 2. It's about as small as details come but also recontextualizes how many – myself included – have viewed Ocarina of Time's fairies for the last 28 years.

"It appears Fairies are just...Fluffy Balls that emit a light!" one Reddit user said . "It's neither a ball of pure light or a humanoid lil person hidden under a glow. Just...Fluff! Interesting :D And cute!"

"Answering the important lore questions like 'is that a sentient puffball or a tiny lady who's so shiny you can only see her aura,'" another fan commented .

Zelda lore is packed with details that fans have obsessed over for decades, so a revelation like this is kind of groundbreaking. Was it always Nintendo's intention for the fairies to be tiny talking puffballs? Probably not, and if you prefer the pure light orb fairies they'll always be there, too, but fans at least seem to have taken to the change after weekend one.

@TAHK0 This is the best thing that’s ever happened to me — Meg (they/them) (@meganroseruiz) November 5, 2026

@TAHK0 This is the best thing that’s ever happened to me

Fairies are far from the only characters making players question their childhood memories. One that more people have realized pre-remake has to do with the attire of Hyrule guards. Don't worry, if it looked to you like they were wearing some pretty standard fantasy knight armor, you'll be happy to know that is exactly what they're wearing in 2026.

"He's wearing f**king jorts?????" one player questioned .

"Yes and he looks great in it," another replied .

So far my favorite part of the Ocarina of Time Remake is that the guards are wearing booty jorts — Cheebs (@ChillboBagginz) November 5, 2026

So far my favorite part of the Ocarina of Time Remake is that the guards are wearing booty jorts

"I like to believe that all the guards are forced to wear jorts under penalty of death, purely because Zelda decrees it so," another Reddit user suggested . "It’s a really nice detail they added in the remake."

Unlike the fairies, it does seem like jorts were standard issue for Zelda's royal guard back in the day. It's just that it's easier to tell that now thanks to the Ocarina of Time remake's Switch 2 graphics. It's made for some funny reactions online, but not all of the new details are quite as charming as jort-wearing knights.

Boundary Break host Shesez, who offers out-of-bounds perspectives on video games, got up close and personal with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's creepiest enemies: the ReDeads. In the N64 game, these mummified zombie grapplers were scary enough thanks to their empty eye sockets. On Switch 2, they still look eyeless – at least at a first glance. Get close (but not too close) enough for a good look, zoom in, and you'll see the developers were nice enough to give ReDead's soulless eyeballs behind their masks. Thanks, Nintendo!

@BoundaryBreak — Vaughn_ers (@Vaughn_ers) November 7, 2026

That's 100% human skull behind that mask," one person said .

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launched last week for Switch 2 and has been picked apart (complimentary) by the internet in just a few days. Dataminers have found potential hints for what could be some exciting new content . Speedrunners have found some game-changing glitches that have produced some hilarious results . Meanwhile, as players get used to their new jump button, Link is going through it .

For more, you can read IGN's review of the game here , or check out our look at the Biggest Changes from the original 1998 game. Be sure to check out our expanding Ocarina of Time remake Walkthrough for comprehensive guides on each main quest area and dungeon, plus where to get Early Heart Pieces, Early Gold Skulltulas , and Early Item Bag Expansions . If you're looking for more, don't miss our complete guides to All Pieces of Heart , All Gold Skulltulas , and All Empty Bottles .
